title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for depression.

HPI
Pt is an 85-year-old female presenting for follow-up of MDD. Pt reports a single episode of depressive symptoms beginning approximately 18 months ago. She describes a persistent low mood, decreased interest in previous hobbies, and significant fatigue. She notes that while she feels "better" than she did at the peak of her symptoms, she still experiences frequent tearfulness and difficulty concentrating on daily tasks. She denies any thoughts of self-harm. Pt reports improved sleep and appetite over the last month. She is currently stable on her current regimen but acknowledges that her mood fluctuates.

Medication List
Sertraline 50mg PO QD
Melatonin 3mg PO HS
Multivitamin PO QD

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Fatigue present, no weight change.
Psychiatric: Depressed mood, tearfulness, decreased concentration. Denies any other symptoms.
Neurological: No tremors, no gait changes.
Respiratory: No SOB, no cough.
Cardiovascular: No chest pain, no palpitations.

Social History
Retired. Lives with her daughter and son-in-law. No tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, stroke.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.
Siblings: One brother, deceased of natural causes.

Vitals
BP: 132/78
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.8%
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
eGFR: 68 mL/min
CBC: WNL

Exam
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears slightly teary but well-groomed.
Psych: Cooperative, speech normal rate/volume. Affect is somewhat constricted. Mood is "okay." Insight and judgment intact.
Physical: CTAB. RRR. Lungs clear. No acute distress.

Assessment
1. Major depressive disorder, single episode. Pt is currently in partial remission. Symptoms are managed but not fully resolved.

Plan
1. Continue Sertraline 50mg QD.
2. Continue current dose of Melatonin for sleep.
3. Continue monitoring mood.
4. Pt to return in 4 weeks for follow-up.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, DO
10/14/2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, single episode, in partial remission (no HCC): F32.4.

distractors.why: The provider documents partial remission: code the remission, not an active severity.
The remission is partial, not full.
